content: [Discord DM kevin_liu Thu Mar 31 14:00 EST 2026] Quick technical note on the Nimbus battery failures. The occlusion detection design spec was 300 mmHg threshold — field reports show the sensor was not reliably detecting partial occlusions below this level in clinical tubing configurations. This is a key root cause for the battery + occlusion combined failure modes. Also the sterile barrier issue is specific to the Nimbus II EpiD and EMS models — the standard Nimbus models had adequate barriers.

Noted: occlusion sensor threshold 300 mmHg design spec — field failures below this threshold. Sterile barrier deficiency limited to Nimbus II EpiD and EMS. Will incorporate in fishbone analysis under Machine (occlusion_sensor) and Material (sterile_barrier) categories.

[Discord DM kevin_liu Thu Mar 31 15:00 EST 2026] On the MDR regulatory requirements — just want to confirm for the compliance section. Manufacturer MDR for death/serious injury: 21 CFR 803.50(a)(1) — 30 calendar days. Urgent/remedial events: 21 CFR 803.53 — 5 work days. Recall reports under 21 CFR Part 806: 10 working days. These should be verbatim in the compliance checklist.

Confirmed verbatim regulatory citations: MDR 30-day: 21 CFR 803.50(a)(1); MDR 5-day urgent: 21 CFR 803.53; Recall report: 21 CFR 806.10 (10 working days). Will use these exact citations in all compliance documentation.
